speaker: Unknown
en: Unless we're telling somebody to go dive with great white sharks, in which case they might get eaten, nobody's going to die from trying to start a business or buy a business and it not working out.
zh: 除非我们是叫人去和大白鲨一起潜水，那种情况下可能会被吃掉，否则没有人会因为尝试创业或者收购一门生意而最终没成而死掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to learn, you're going to go through difficulty, it might be really hard, you might fail.
zh: 你会学到东西，你会经历困难，可能会非常艰难，你可能会失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you probably won't stand at your grave at the end of the day and say, thank God I took no risk, I stayed in a job I hated, and I never actually went and stood out at the front of anything.
zh: 但在生命尽头，你大概率不会站在自己的坟墓前说：谢天谢地我没冒任何风险，我一直待在一份我讨厌的工作里，我从来没有真正站到过任何事情的最前线。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's Cody Sanchez, founder and CEO of finance and media company Contrarian Thinking.
zh: 这位是 Cody Sanchez，金融与媒体公司 Contrarian Thinking 的创始人兼 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: With stock market valuations high and the job market tight, Cody argues in her new book, Own or Be Owned, that taking control of your financial future right now requires investing in yourself.
zh: 在股市估值高企、就业市场紧缩的背景下，Cody 在她的新书《Own or Be Owned》中主张，现在就要掌控你的财务未来，需要投资于你自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: Her impassioned plea for building or buying your own small business includes hardcore data about what turns risk into opportunity.
zh: 她关于创建或收购自己小企业的激情呼吁，包含了关于什么能把风险转化为机遇的硬核数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And her advice translates even if you do work for someone else, decrying what she calls cowboying in business as a key pitfall.
zh: 即使你是为别人工作的，她的建议也同样适用，她抨击了她所说的商业中的“cowboying”（鲁莽行事）是一个关键的陷阱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's get to it.
zh: 那么让我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Bob Safian, and this is Rapid Response.
zh: 我是 Bob Safian，这里是 Rapid Response。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, listeners, Bob Safian here.
zh: 嘿，各位听众，我是 Bob Safian。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we get into today's episode, I want to introduce you to Eli Wallen, founder and CEO of Engine.
zh: 在进入今天的节目之前，我想向你介绍 Eli Wallen，Engine 的创始人兼 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: Engine is a sponsor of the show, which is something we're very grateful for.
zh: Engine 是本节目的赞助商，对此我们非常感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome, Eli.
zh: 欢迎，Eli。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks so much for having me, Bob.
zh: 非常感谢你邀请我，Bob。

speaker: Unknown
en: How is AI impacting how people book, manage, and finance travel today?
zh: 如今 AI 正在如何影响人们预订、管理和为旅行融资？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how far along the progress curve are we?
zh: 我们在进步曲线上走到多远了？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's still very, very early.
zh: 现在还非常非常早。

speaker: Unknown
en: The larger corporations, the bigger businesses, they really have not had a lot of opportunity to adopt AI yet in a meaningful way, kind of primarily because of the legacy systems that are still trying to catch up.
zh: 那些更大的企业、更大的公司，它们实际上还没有太多机会以有意义的方式采用 AI，主要原因是那些仍在努力追赶的遗留系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say on the consumer side, you've seen more, you've seen people at least book trips, but for the most part, it's still quite nascent.
zh: 我想说的是，在消费者端，你已经看到了更多，你看到人们至少会预订行程，但在大多数情况下，它仍处于相当初期的阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of times these are big ticket items and relying on just an LLM to do that blindly and just kind of take your hands off and just let the agent run and book.
zh: 很多时候这些都是大额消费项目，仅盲目依赖一个 LLM 来做这件事，就放手不管，让智能体自行运行和预订，

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's too much nuance.
zh: 我认为其中有太多细微差别。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's too much change potentially can come up.
zh: 可能会出现太多变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you're building engine and the engine experience, do you assume your customers will be AI agents?
zh: 在你构建 Engine 和 Engine 体验的过程中，你假设你的客户会是 AI 智能体吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like is a service for AI agents different than one for humans?
zh: 也就是说，面向 AI 智能体的服务与面向人类的服务不同吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you navigate that?
zh: 你如何应对这个问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: Our customers can connect and start to glean insights and understand what's going on with their travel program from their LLM directly.
zh: 我们的客户可以连接并开始直接从他们的 LLM 中获取洞察，了解他们的差旅项目正在发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I don't think the industry has quite yet caught up to maybe the expectations of what buyers have to where the capabilities of the technology
zh: 但我认为这个行业还没有完全跟上买家期望与技术能力之间的差距

speaker: Unknown
en: So what makes Engine distinctive among the tech tools that people could use for their travel planning?
zh: 那么在人们可以用于旅行规划的各种科技工具中，是什么让 Engine 独树一帜？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we were not cut from the travel cloth, so to speak.
zh: 你知道，可以说我们并非出身于旅行行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think the way that we built this, for the last eight years, we've been working on the infrastructure.
zh: 所以我认为我们构建这套系统的方式，在过去八年里，我们一直在做基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: And kind of the underlying network of suppliers and content and rates and all of these things that put us in a very strong position today, which is, you know, a modern infrastructure platform that AI can sit on top of travel management, travel policies, approvals.
zh: 还有底层的供应商、内容、价格等所有这些东西的网络，这让我们今天处于一个非常有利的位置，也就是一个现代的基础设施平台，AI 可以坐在上面，还有差旅管理、差旅政策、审批。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was all kind of what makes the most sense versus what was done before.
zh: 这些都大致上是最合理的做法，而不是以前那些做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's given us the ability to create something more modern that people are looking for versus trying to repeat kind of the past structure of some of those more legacy platforms.
zh: 我认为这让我们有能力创造出人们正在寻找的更现代的东西，而不是试图重复那些更遗留平台的过往结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: Eli, thank you so much for joining me today and sharing more about what makes Engine unique.
zh: Eli，非常感谢你今天加入我，并分享更多关于 Engine 独特之处的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a pleasure.
zh: 很荣幸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really appreciate it.
zh: 真的很感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now on to today's show.
zh: 现在进入今天的节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Bob Safian.
zh: 我是 Bob Safian。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm here with Cody Sanchez, founder and CEO of finance and media company, Contrary in Thinking.
zh: 我在这里和 Cody Sanchez 在一起，她是金融与媒体公司 Contrary in Thinking 的创始人兼 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cody, welcome back to the show.
zh: Cody，欢迎回到节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for having me.
zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thrilled to be here.
zh: 很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were last a guest in 2024, talking about your book, Main Street Millionaire.
zh: 你上一次做客是 2024 年，谈的是你的书《Main Street Millionaire》。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've now got a new book coming with a more aggressive title, Own or Be Owned.
zh: 你现在有一本新书即将出版，书名更有攻击性，《Own or Be Owned》。

speaker: Unknown
en: It sounds like an ultimatum.
zh: 这听起来像是一个最后通牒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that the choice we face today?
zh: 这是我们今天面临的选择吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you know, we actually thought a lot about this title because it is aggressive.
zh: 是的，你知道，我们实际上对这个书名考虑了很多，因为它确实很有攻击性。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really aggressive to say that if you don't own things, then somebody else is in charge of you, you know?
zh: 说如果你不拥有东西，那么别人就支配着你，这真的非常具有攻击性，你知道吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: There are many connotations to that.
zh: 这有很多层含义。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what I've realized as an owner is, first of all, you can own things and be owned by it.
zh: 但作为拥有者，我意识到的是，首先，你可以拥有东西，却反而被它所拥有。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've now worked with somewhere around 15,000 small business owners.
zh: 我们现在已经和大约 15000 名小企业主打过交道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of them are owned by those businesses.
zh: 他们中的大多数拥有这些企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of them do not have an exit.
zh: 他们中的大多数人没有退出计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: And most small businesses are not profitable.
zh: 而且大多数小企业并不盈利。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the last book I did, the whole point was go and buy a profitable small business so we don't get owned by Wall Street and everything looks like Walmart.
zh: 所以我上一本书的全部要点就是去买一家盈利的小企业，这样我们就不会被华尔街拥有，一切看起来都像沃尔玛。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then once we realized this, wow, we had taught thousands of people how to buy a business and I always say congratulations and I'm sorry because this part kind of sucks.
zh: 然后当我们意识到这一点时，哇，我们已经教了成千上万的人如何买一家企业，而我总是说祝贺你，也很抱歉，因为这部分有点糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now it was like, how do we get them to run profitable businesses that you don't hate, that don't make you miserable every day?
zh: 所以现在问题变成了：我们如何让他们经营盈利的企业，而且是你不会讨厌的、不会让你每天都痛苦的企业？

speaker: Unknown
en: And just to be clear, can you work for someone else and not be owned?
zh: 先说清楚一点：你可以为别人工作而不被拥有吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, yeah.
zh: 哦，当然可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the cool part about this book is I don't think everybody should be an owner.
zh: 我的意思是，这本书很酷的一点是，我不认为每个人都应该当老板。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think everybody should own some parts of companies.
zh: 我认为每个人都应该拥有公司的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure, you can do it through equities, but I think as an employee in a company, you can get shares of the company.
zh: 当然，你可以通过股票来实现，但我认为作为公司的员工，你可以获得公司的股份。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can do rev share splits.
zh: 你可以做收入分成。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can do profit sharing.
zh: 你可以做利润分成。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you understand how businesses make money, you can figure out how to negotiate your cut of it.
zh: 如果你理解企业是怎么赚钱的，你就能想清楚怎么谈判你应得的那一份。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, no, I think there's many days.
zh: 所以，不是的，我认为有很多日子。

speaker: Unknown
en: You catch me on the wrong day, Bob.
zh: 你要是赶上我状态不好的那天，Bob。

speaker: Unknown
en: I might say, I'll come work for you, you know?
zh: 我可能会说，我来给你打工吧，你懂的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the last time we talked, you said that our country might be less of a tragedy if we all owned a piece of it, that we would care more about making it better.
zh: 我的意思是，上次我们聊的时候，你说如果我们国家每个人都拥有它的一部分，它可能就没那么悲惨了，我们会更在意让它变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, owning a piece, it could be owning your own business.
zh: 所以，拥有一部分，可以是拥有你自己的企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be owning shares in the stock market.
zh: 可以是拥有股市里的股票。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be owning a home.
zh: 可以是拥有一套房子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, is all ownership equally, what's the right word, motivational?
zh: 就是说，是不是所有形式的「拥有」都同样，该怎么说呢，有激励性？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, well, I mean, I don't have any data to support this, so that would be, I'm not sure exactly quantifiably, but the difference with owning part of a business that you are a part of is you have some control over the outcome.
zh: 是的，嗯，我没有数据支持这个说法，所以在量化的层面上我不太确定，但拥有一家你身在其中、有份参与的企业，不同之处在于你对结果有一定的控制权。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, if you own a stock, you're making a bet on somebody else's ability to continue to build.
zh: 你知道，如果你持有某只股票，你是在押注别人持续构建的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you own a house, you're betting on the housing market, and then you have to move if you want to realize any of those gains.
zh: 如果你有房子，你是在押注房地产市场，而且如果你想实现任何增值，你就得搬走。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you own part of the business that you work in or part of businesses that you work alongside, you can actually affect the outcome.
zh: 当你拥有你所在企业的部分，或者你共同工作企业的部分时，你实际上可以影响结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is really inspiring because it makes you want to work harder.
zh: 这真的非常鼓舞人心，因为它让你想要更努力地工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just because I own Apple, my day-to-day has no impact on what Apple is going to do.
zh: 仅仅因为我持有苹果的股票，我的日常工作对苹果会做什么没有任何影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you own part of your business that you're integrating, well, you're not going to burn down the house that you were trying to build.
zh: 如果你拥有你参与的那部分企业，那么，你不会烧掉你自己正在努力建造的房子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think about that sort of all around our world.
zh: 所以我会围绕我们这个世界方方面面来思考这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And can we just get little parts of these businesses too if we don't want to take on the big risk of owning the whole thing?
zh: 那如果我们不想承担拥有整个企业的大风险，我们能不能也拿到这些企业的小部分？

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you're, I don't know, when you're deciding where to invest your money, I guess, and your time, but really your money, like you would prioritize a business over, say, owning your own home over individual stocks, although people have made a ton of money on stocks lately.
zh: 当你在，我不知道，当你在决定把钱投到哪里的时候，我猜，还有你的时间，但主要是你的钱，你会把投资一家企业放在优先位置，比如说，优先于拥有自己的房子、优先于买个股，尽管最近很多人在股票上赚了大钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you know, you have to have a lot of money to make money in the stock market.
zh: 是的，你知道，你要有很多钱才能在股市里赚到钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an incredible wealth accelerator once you have capital to invest.
zh: 一旦你有了可投资的资本，它是一个不可思议的财富加速器。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ownership in a business is one of the very few things where you can actually trade your time for long-term dollars.
zh: 拥有企业的一部分是为数不多的几件事之一，你真的可以用你的时间换长期美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a bias that I think more people should bet on themselves.
zh: 我有一个偏向，我认为更多人应该押注自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll figure out what they're capable of and then also be able to make more because of it.
zh: 他们会弄清楚自己能做什么，并因此也能赚得更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also the only investment that even if you lose, you win because you can take some experience from it.
zh: 这也是唯一一种即使输了也是赢的投资，因为你可以从中学到一些经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you YOLO into Robinhood, okay, maybe you learn to not buy at the top or to not buy in market hype cycles, but what is your real learning experience?
zh: 如果你在 Robinhood 上梭哈，好吧，也许你学会了不要在顶部买入，或者不要在市场炒作周期中买入，但你真正学到的东西是什么呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think in businesses, you get that.
zh: 而在企业里，你能得到那种经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: As far as owning a home or not, I think that's usually an emotional purchase, which I totally understand.
zh: 至于要不要拥有房子，我认为那通常是一种情绪化的购买，这一点我完全理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it feels special.
zh: 就是说它感觉很特别。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it's such a core part of like the American dream.
zh: 因为它是美国梦如此核心的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: You sort of feel like it doesn't really need to be.
zh: 你多少会觉得它其实不需要是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's really just another liability that you have to pay for every single month and that holds you to a job maybe that you don't like or something that you are not sure you want to do.
zh: 是的，它真的只是你每个月都得付钱的另一笔负债，而且它把你拴在一份你也许不喜欢的工作上，或者一件你不确定自己想做的事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when you have a lot of money, great, own houses.
zh: 所以当你有很多钱的时候，很好，去拥有房子吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know that sounds elitist, but when you don't have a lot of money, I would bet on yourself all day and increase your cash flow so nobody can own you.
zh: 我知道这听起来很精英主义，但当你没有很多钱的时候，我会整天都押注你自己，提高你的现金流，这样就没有人能拥有你。

speaker: Unknown
en: You alluded to this when you talked about sort of the motivation for this book versus the first book.
zh: 你在谈到这本书与第一本书的动机差异时提到过这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, owning a business can trap you as easily as it frees you.
zh: 就是说，拥有一家企业让你获得自由的同时，也同样容易困住你。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know the founders I talk to, I'm sure you hear this all the time, too.
zh: 我认识的那些创始人，我相信你也经常听到这样的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, if I'd known how hard it was, I never would have started this.
zh: 比如，要是我早知道这么难，我根本就不会开始做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, is it better sometimes not to know how hard it is?
zh: 你说，有时候不知道它有多难是不是反而更好？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well...

speaker: Unknown
en: One, I think that we have all gotten sort of trauma bonded over entrepreneurship.
zh: 第一，我觉得我们所有人都在创业这件事上形成了某种创伤纽带。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't sound very fun if I come on here and say, actually, business is going pretty good.
zh: 如果我上节目说，其实生意做得挺不错的，那听起来就不太好玩了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're making a lot of money.
zh: 我们赚了很多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm having a good time.
zh: 我过得很开心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Things are going well.
zh: 一切都很顺利。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of gross.
zh: 唯一难的地方在于，即兴发挥和随意尝试更有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's almost like the reverse of the casino.
zh: 所以这几乎是赌场的反面。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the casino, they only tell you when they win.
zh: 在赌场，他们只告诉你他们赢钱的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: In business, they only really like talking about the difficulty or hardships or when they've raised a bunch of outside venture capital.
zh: 在生意场上，人们真正喜欢谈论的只有困难、艰辛，或者他们融了一大笔外部风险投资的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think for most small business owners, yes, it's hard, but they kind of love the game.
zh: 所以我觉得对大多数小企业主来说，是的，很难，但他们其实挺热爱这个游戏的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it's an addictive game to play.
zh: 这是个让人上瘾的游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is that they aren't profitable.
zh: 问题在于他们并不盈利。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything's more fun when you're making money.
zh: 赚钱的时候，一切都会变得更有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if the average small business owner makes $65,000 a year, well, that's less than minimum wage in California and less than even the median income in the US.
zh: 如果普通小企业主年收入是 6.5 万美元，那比加州的最低工资还低，甚至低于美国的中位数收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we've got to figure out how to have profitable businesses because then the pain and difficulty is a lot easier to manage.
zh: 所以我们得搞清楚怎么让生意盈利，因为那样的话，痛苦和困难就容易应对得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the, I don't know, the mistakes or the traps that folks who are, you know, running their own businesses are running themselves into?
zh: 那些……我不知道，自己经营生意的人容易掉进去的错误或陷阱是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not that they're not working hard.

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm not sure how that is helpful at all.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 完美的例子。

en: There's this, it's an HVAC company and commercial and based in Florida.
zh: 有这么一家公司，是一家 HVAC 公司，做商用，总部在佛罗里达。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the guy is like, well, you know, I'm working on this AI integration and it's going here and it's been pretty incredible.
zh: 那家伙说：你看，我正在做这个 AI 集成，它要用在这里，效果相当惊人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I just said, can I have your phone number for your business?
zh: 然后我就说：能给我你们公司的电话号码吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I call the business.
zh: 我打了那家公司的电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's Friday.
zh: 那是周五。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like 10, 15 in the morning.
zh: 大概上午 10 点 15 分左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: I call the business.
zh: 我打了那家公司的电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody answers.
zh: 没人接。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is, I kid you not, an AI special jingle the guy made.
zh: 我不骗你，有一段那家伙自己做的 AI 特别铃声。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really cute.
zh: 挺可爱的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it goes to a voicemail.
zh: 然后就转到了语音信箱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, guy.
zh: 我就想，哥们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go and what is this voicemail?
zh: 然后，这语音信箱是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Get an answering service.
zh: 找一个电话应答服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just lost a commercial client potentially.
zh: 你可能刚刚失去了一个商业客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are we doing?
zh: 我们这是在干什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so sometimes when you're the business owner, you have too many things.
zh: 所以有时候当你自己是企业主的时候，你有太多的事情要做。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need somebody to go like, that right there is where the money is.
zh: 你需要有人来跟你说，就是那里，钱就在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just do that.
zh: 就做那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you can layer the cute stuff on top of it later.
zh: 然后那些花哨的东西以后再叠加在上面。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our methodology overall is like, you're kind of overcomplicating it and that's okay.
zh: 所以我们整体的方法论就是，你有点把它过度复杂化了，但这没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: We all do it.
zh: 我们都会这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's go back to boring.
zh: 我们回到无聊的做法吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: It actually works really well.
zh: 它其实非常有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: You personally have had a lot of success within the creator economy of millions of followers across platforms.
zh: 你个人在创作者经济中取得了很大的成功，在各个平台上有数百万粉丝。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is building a personal brand now sort of an economic necessity for everyone, for every business?
zh: 建立个人品牌现在对每个人、每个企业来说是不是一种经济上的必要？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I do not think most small businesses should build a personal brand at all.
zh: 不，我认为大多数小企业完全不应该建立个人品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did it by accident during COVID because I was stuck at home and I started with a newsletter and I liked writing and then I had fun creating.
zh: 我是在疫情期间无意中做到的，因为我被困在家里，我从一个时事通讯开始，我喜欢写作，然后我觉得创作很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, this is fun.
zh: 我当时想，这很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I just wanted to optimize for making money,
zh: 如果我只是想优化赚钱这件事，

speaker: Unknown
en: I would not do this.
zh: 我不会做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, and there's cool parts to it.
zh: 你知道，这其中有很酷的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, don't get me wrong.
zh: 别误会我的意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's very cool parts.
zh: 有非常酷的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I get to have lovely conversations with you.
zh: 我可以和你进行愉快的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I get to go on Good Morning America.
zh: 你知道，我可以上《早安美国》。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's very, like, ego satisfying, for sure.
zh: 那确实非常，怎么说呢，让人自我满足。

speaker: Unknown
en: But most small businesses don't make money off of their personal brands.
zh: 但大多数小企业并不能靠他们的个人品牌赚钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, if you knew what most of the YouTubers actually make, you know, the sprinkler guy down the road makes like 5X.
zh: 我是说，如果你知道大多数 YouTuber 实际上赚多少钱，你知道，你家附近那个做洒水系统的人赚的大概是他们的 5 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't make that much money.
zh: 他们赚不到那么多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's really hard to stay relevant forever.
zh: 而且要永远保持热度真的很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it won't be too far in the future where people won't care at all about me anymore.
zh: 比如说，用不了多久，人们就会完全不再关心我了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's okay because I have these other businesses, but you don't want to create a business of you.
zh: 而这没关系，因为我有这些其他的企业，但你不会想把生意做成完全围绕你自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, no, relevance is an exhausting and difficult track to stay on.
zh: 是啊，没错，保持热度是一条令人精疲力尽且艰难的赛道。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you gotta have a thick skin, too.
zh: 而且你还得有厚脸皮。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've seen growing media coverage around hands-on jobs that can't be displaced by AI.
zh: 我们看到越来越多的媒体报道关于那些不会被 AI 取代的动手类工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're considering a small business right now,
zh: 当你现在考虑做一门小生意的时候，

speaker: Unknown
en: Are those the kind of industries you should be leaning towards?
zh: 那些是不是你应该偏向选择的行业类型？

speaker: Unknown
en: If I had to look at the top industries right now, I would say, first of all, anything in manufacturing.
zh: 如果要我看现在最好的行业，我会说，首先，任何制造业相关的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a ton of grants and a ton of opportunity to reshore back to the US right now.
zh: 现在有大量的补助金，也有大量的机会把业务迁回美国。

speaker: Unknown
en: Home services, a massive shortage.
zh: 家政服务，严重短缺。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then I would go to more of the skilled trades.
zh: 然后我会说更多是技术工种。

speaker: Unknown
en: You do have to go, you know, to some sort of trade school, but the pay is actually quite high.
zh: 你确实需要去，你知道，上某种职业技校，但薪资其实相当高。

speaker: Unknown
en: People will say,
zh: 人们会说，

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, ugh, but a plumber, you know, he's never gonna make...
zh: 唉，可是水管工，你知道，他永远也赚不到……

speaker: Unknown
zh: 一年 30 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: He might make $125,000 a year.
zh: 他可能一年赚 12.5 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that misses the point.
zh: 但这没有抓住重点。

speaker: Unknown
en: As a skilled tradesman, your ability to then go buy a plumbing business is so much higher than anybody else's.
zh: 作为一名技术工人，你之后去买下一家管道公司的可能性比任何其他人都高得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: The world seems pretty chaotic right now.
zh: 现在的世界看起来相当混乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Political uncertainty, trade war with Canada, oil prices.
zh: 政治不确定性，与加拿大的贸易战，油价。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it might make people feel like now is not the time to take on new risks, that we need to just focus on what we control right in front of us and sort of stay here and not change anything.
zh: 我是说，这可能会让人觉得现在不是承担新风险的时候，我们只需要专注于眼前我们能控制的事情，就待在这里，不做任何改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you say to that impulse?
zh: 对于这种冲动你会怎么说？

speaker: Unknown
en: That the world has actually never been better in most ways.
zh: 事实上,这个世界在大多数方面从未如此好过。

speaker: Unknown
en: I always go like, is it a feeling or is that the math?
zh: 我总是会问,这是一种感觉,还是数据说的?

speaker: Unknown
en: And the math says, writ large, we live longer, we're wealthier on average than we've ever been before, we have more opportunities than we've ever had before.
zh: 而数据总体上说的是,我们活得更久了,我们平均比以往任何时候都更富有,我们拥有比以往任何时候都更多的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you live in a developed country, even though in some ways it is harder, aka
zh: 而且如果你生活在一个发达国家,尽管在某些方面确实更难了,也就是说

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, houses are more expensive.
zh: 你知道的,房子更贵了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Groceries might be more expensive.
zh: 食品杂货可能更贵了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of those not so small things are harder.
zh: 有些不那么小的东西变得更难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also never been simpler in a lot of ways to get wealthy.
zh: 但在很多方面,致富也从未如此简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I would say don't ever let market economics or somebody else labeling you a victim or the time as not being right now stop you from making it your time right now.
zh: 所以我想说,永远不要让市场经济、或者别人给你贴上受害者的标签、或者觉得时机不对,阻止你让现在成为你的时机。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because people will win in every market.
zh: 因为在每一个市场里都会有人赢。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just, are you going to decide to be one of them or not?
zh: 只是,你打算不打算决定成为其中之一?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and time is the one thing we don't have an unlimited amount of, right?
zh: 是的,而时间是我们唯一没有无限量供应的东西,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why would you ever let somebody tell you that you can't just because it is hard right now or it is chaotic?
zh: 你为什么要让别人告诉你不行,只因为现在很难或者很混乱?

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, yes, and you're probably more capable than you've given yourself credit for, and you're not going to listen to the people who tell you that it's possible for somebody else but not for you.
zh: 你知道的,是的,你很可能比你自认为的更有能力,而且你不要去听那些人说这事对别人可能、对你不行。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I don't believe that.
zh: 不,我不相信那种说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, Cody, this was great.
zh: 好的,Cody,这期很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks so much for doing it.
zh: 非常感谢你来参加。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you guys for taking the time and covering it.
zh: 谢谢你们抽出时间来做这个报道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really appreciate it.
zh: 我非常感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love Cody's optimism amidst all the tumult in today's world.
zh: 我喜欢 Cody 在当今世界种种动荡之中保持的乐观。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll confess, I can get distracted by all the troubling headlines, and it's good to be reminded of the positives.
zh: 我得承认,我容易被那些令人不安的新闻标题分散注意力,被人提醒一下那些积极的事情是好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also good to remember that the only time given to us is right now.
zh: 记住我们唯一被给予的时间就是当下,这也是好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So why not make the most of it?
zh: 那为什么不充分利用它呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think a sense of ownership changes how you view the world and how you view your work.
zh: 我确实认为,一种所有权感会改变你看待世界的方式和你看待自己工作的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: For me, I don't necessarily need to be the quote unquote owner of a business to have that feeling, but I appreciate that everyone is different.
zh: 对我来说,我不一定非要成为一个企业名义上的“所有者”才能有那种感觉,但我理解每个人都不同。

en: As for buying a business, starting a business, Cody's underlying message is to craft your ownership, your career based on your own proclivities and goals.

zh: 你想要的是一种生活方式、一次退出、还是一场规模化之旅?

zh: 成功始于对自己诚实。
